---
title: Plain English
type: docs
---

This page deliberately has no internal headings. It still contains enough text
to exercise whole-document progress synchronization when the two translations
have no shared anchors.

The first passage is intentionally long enough to make the reading surface
scrollable. A translation can use different line lengths and paragraph sizes,
so the reader should follow document progress rather than pretend that every
line has a counterpart.

The second passage repeats the same idea with more words in the source page.
The comparison view should keep both panes moving from the beginning to the
end while showing the approximate nature of the estimate beside Sync scroll.

The final passage gives the page a reachable bottom edge. It exists to make
the interpolation visible in a browser test and to keep this fixture focused
on pages that are text without section anchors.

The reader remains useful even when a content author chooses prose without
headings. The two documents retain their ordinary HTML and are only placed
side by side by the temporary browser reader.

More plain text keeps this fixture intentionally heading-less while making
the scroll range unambiguous. The source can contain explanatory paragraphs,
examples, caveats, and transitions without a single section marker. The
comparison reader should still offer a useful estimate based on the bounded
progress through the full document.

The translation may be shorter in one paragraph and longer in another. There
is no safe local anchor to use, so the full-document estimate is the honest
fallback. The warning beside Sync scroll tells the reader why the alignment
is approximate without covering either document with a banner.

This final block adds a little more space below the preceding text. It keeps
the bottom of the page reachable and makes the midpoint test meaningful on a
small viewport. The content itself is deliberately ordinary prose so the
fixture does not accidentally introduce a heading through a shortcode.
